key_insight: Minimal-Witness Reinforcement Learning (MWRL) learns not just one valid solution, but the full family of minimal sufficient witnesses by assigning credit based on each proposal’s unique contribution to the union of successful outcomes.
engineering_relevance: This matters for theorem proving and other verifier-driven systems because it can reduce redundant solutions and recover diverse minimal proofs or explanations from only binary verifier feedback.
method: Treats minimal-witness search as a reinforcement learning problem over verifier-accepted proposals
Credits each proposal by how much coverage the group union would lose without it
Provides both a value-iteration planner for exhaustive witness recovery and a policy-gradient variant scalable to large language models
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments across multiple settings where MWRL recovers most minimal witnesses, while baselines often produce redundant supersets or only a single witness.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and sparsity of verifier feedback, and the approach may still miss some witnesses when the search space is large or proposals are poorly explored.
